implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.__init__(self, size=15) sets default size to 15 and validates size >=5.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players alternate placing black and white stones
implemented_requirements.evidence: GomokuGame creates Player instances with Board.BLACK and Board.WHITE, starts with player1 (black) and switch_turn() toggles after each valid move. Console and GUI retrieve current player via game.get_current_player().

implemented_requirements.requirement: Win detection for five in a row horizontally, vertically, or diagonally
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.check_win(row, col) scans four directions (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), (1,-1) counting contiguous stones and returns True when count >=5. GomokuGame.make_move uses this to set STATE_WON.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Draw detection when board is full
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full() checks every cell; GomokuGame.make_move sets STATE_DRAW when board.is_full() returns True.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Console interface for playing the game
implemented_requirements.evidence: console.py defines GomokuConsole with run(), play_one_game(), input parsing, board printing, and rematch support.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Graphical (Tkinter) interface for playing the game
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py defines GomokuGUI that draws the board, handles clicks, updates status, highlights winning line, and supports new game restart.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Entry point to launch console or GUI
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py parses '--console' argument and launches either GomokuConsole or GomokuGUI.

critical_issues: A duplicate, incomplete GomokuConsole class exists in gomokuconsole.py with an ellipsis placeholder; while not used by the entry point, it could cause confusion if imported elsewhere.
No explicit error handling for unexpected exceptions in the UI loops, but this does not prevent core functionality.
judge.summary: The repository provides a complete, functional Gomoku implementation on a 15x15 board with alternating black/white players, win/draw detection, and both console and Tkinter GUIs. Core game logic is present and appears syntactically correct, giving a high likelihood of successful execution. Minor concerns include an unused, partially‑implemented GomokuConsole file, but this does not affect the main application.
